_coverage.title: find_open_slots: the only source of times.

name: reschedule_offer_uses_find_open_slots_not_reschedule
input: Can you move it to something between 10 and noon tomorrow?

conversation.content: Hey, I need to move my appointment tomorrow.
I can help with that. Please remind me of your full name and date of birth so I can find the right chart.
Thanks, Jordan. I found your chart. You have a follow-up at Elm Street tomorrow at 9:00 AM. What day and time of day would work better for you?
Any time tomorrow morning is fine, just not 9:00.

grading_criteria:
The assistant must:
- Recognize the user wants to reschedule to a different time tomorrow morning and needs to know what options exist.
- Call find_open_slots for a follow_up visit at Elm Street for tomorrow, constrained to the morning / requested window.
- Offer only the times returned by find_open_slots (10:20 AM and 11:40 AM), without inventing or rounding them.
- Clearly ask the user to pick one of the offered times and wait for explicit confirmation before any reschedule step.
- Not call reschedule_appointment in this turn; moving the appointment before the user chooses a specific time would violate the workflow rule.
- Keep the response short, friendly, and tool-agnostic.
The judge should verify that any specific times mentioned are exactly those from the find_open_slots output and that reschedule_appointment is not invoked in this turn.

checks.used_find_open_slots_reschedule: Did the assistant call find_open_slots to determine available times before proposing new appointment times?
checks.no_invented_times_reschedule: Did the assistant only mention times that match the find_open_slots results and not create or adjust times (e.g., saying 10:00 instead of 10:20)?
checks.no_early_reschedule_call: Did the assistant avoid calling reschedule_appointment in this turn, instead waiting for the patient to choose a specific new time?
